column3: BSB’s “Paul” matches the Textus Receptus (Παῦλος); the critical text has only “he.”
“Paul” specifies the unexpressed subject of went to them.
“Heads” is plural where the Greek has singular head; “of it” is supplied.
“Paul” and “the synagogue” specify the subject and from there; “Titus Justus” replaces Titius Justus.
The purpose to harm you is not expressed.
“Paul” and “the Corinthians” specify he and them.
“Speak” replaces open his mouth; “your complaint” is supplied.
“A dispute about words” replaces plural questions about a word.
“Corinth” is supplied; “to keep a vow he had made” states a purpose where the Greek says he had a vow.
“Paul” and “Priscilla and Aquila” specify the unexpressed subject and them.
